claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but low ductility because stress concentrates at its incoherent interfaces.
Applying 6 GPa at 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the original FCC/B2 lamellae.
The HPHT treatment will create a hierarchical microstructure with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent interfaces in the transformed alloy will promote dislocation transfer across phase boundaries.
The transformed structure will promote stacking-fault formation.
The transformed structure will promote deformation twinning.
Dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning will produce a homogeneous strain distribution and arrest interfacial cracking.
In a W-based refractory HEA, dislocations shear across coherent lamellar boundaries and generate approximately 40% local shear without crack initiation, alleviating local stress concentration.
HPHT treatment reduces interfacial energy and promotes atomic diffusion.
HPHT-driven reduction of interfacial energy and enhanced diffusion transform incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent ones.
Synergistic twinning and transformation-induced plasticity enable the treated alloy to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The treated alloy will attain fracture strain greater than 10% while retaining strength greater than 1500 MPa.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated cracks and extensive plastic deformation rather than isolated microcracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain, indicating homogeneous deformation.
The baseline as-cast or homogenized alloy exhibits brittle fracture with isolated microcracks.
The baseline alloy has a heterogeneous GND distribution, with high density at interfaces and low density within grains.

The pressure and temperature must exceed the threshold for topological transformation and interface coherence while remaining below conditions that cause melting, amorphization, other phase instability, or excessive grain coarsening.
Pressure treatment may induce an alternative phase transformation, such as BCC-to-HCP, instead of the desired coherent topology.
